I farm 12 mu, not a big place, so I cannot take big risks. I do what has worked on my land. Wheat and maize together keep the family steady. If one side is weak, the other can still bring something back. I have a well, so I will still irrigate, but pumping water costs money, so I will not water for no reason. Some people in my house work outside, so labor is tight at busy times. Because of that, for wheat I keep things the usual way, and for maize I rush to plant right after wheat harvest and do less tillage. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go hungry, but I still have to watch cash, so I use round amounts, same as the last years that were acceptable.

For wheat, I will sow in early October on the full 12 mu, using the seed people around here usually buy from the local dealer, not the cheapest saved seed. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts to stand up and grow strong. If the field stays dry, I will irrigate about three times: once after sowing if moisture is short, once around jointing, and once around grain filling if needed. For maize, after I cut wheat in June, I will plant quickly on the same 12 mu. That gap is short, so I will not waste time with heavy plowing. I will use hybrid maize seed, put some fertilizer early, then give another dose when the maize is knee-high to waist-high. Usually rain helps maize, so I plan one irrigation, maybe two if summer turns dry. That is enough for my land if the season is normal.
